claims.claim: Reviewers describe the puzzles as challenging and requiring players to think carefully.

citations.review_text: Very fun, challenging, overall good game.
Humor is amazing, puzzles are challenging, the voice acting is funny, and the music adds to it all! Seriously try this game (please!).

I can't believe it took me over 15 years to put the time in to completing Portal 2. It's an absolute joy to play with exceptional writing and voice acting, especially by Stephen Merchant as Wheatley, who had me laughing out loud countless times with his delivery of some very funny lines. The puzzles themselves get progressively more difficult as you get in to the game and you get a real sense of achievement once you crack the tougher ones. An absolute pleasure to play and I wish more modern-day games developers took note of this absolute classic in how to perfect their craft.

An unforgettable classic and a massive sequel to one of the best titles ever in gaming. 

Extremely well designed, the atmosphere and maps are all grand and it makes you realize on how big of a building you are in, you're able to see more than just the test chambers and, yeah, Portal 1 isn't able to make you fathom as much as Portal 2 does about how massive the whole facility really is.

Writing is top-notch, the lore is laid out throughout the entire game through posters, dialogues, prerecorded messages, puzzles, everywhere. Voice actors did an extraordinary job immersing you and making the game feel alive, I love how many voice lines there are.

About the puzzles... they're really awesome, they get harder the more you progress, yet, with enough observation, you never quite feel like you're lost, you're able to get through it all just by yourself. New mechanics are always interesting to see and one of my favourites were the gels, they add more variety to what puzzles you can make and it would've been a pity if the gel concept were scrapped forever. While still on gameplay, the co-op mode? Undoubtedly worth it with friends, it's so damn fun.

Need I say a word about the music? Nothing but praise comes out of my fingers as I am writing this, 'Want You Gone' and 'Still Alive' have cemented themselves as one of the most recognizable, loved, and fitting songs in the history of gaming.

Overall, this series, and especially Portal 2, is a must-play. 10/10.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Incremental mechanics and workshop support sustain long-term engagement and coordinated play.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a separate cooperative campaign that requires communication and coordination with another player.

citations.review_text:
Portal 2 is a perfect example of how a relatively simple idea can turn into an unforgettable gaming experience.

The main mechanic is easy to understand: you use a portal gun to create connections between different surfaces and solve puzzles by manipulating space, momentum and physics. However, the game constantly finds new ways to challenge your thinking without making the experience feel unnecessarily complicated.

What really makes Portal 2 stand out is its presentation. The writing is genuinely funny, the characters are memorable, and the conversations between GLaDOS, Wheatley and the player make even the quieter moments entertaining.

The puzzle design is another highlight. New mechanics are introduced gradually, and the game does an excellent job of teaching you through experimentation rather than constantly explaining everything.

There is also a separate cooperative campaign, which is a fantastic addition. Solving puzzles with another player introduces a completely different experience and requires actual communication and coordination.

Even years after release, Portal 2 remains incredibly enjoyable. Its combination of clever puzzles, humor, atmosphere and excellent level design makes it one of the most memorable puzzle games on Steam.

If you haven't played it yet, you're missing out on something special.

Portal 2 takes everything that made the original great and builds it into a full and confident adventure. The core idea is simple that you place two linked portals and use them to get through puzzles. But the game keeps adding new tools at a steady pace such as light bridges, tractor beams and paint like gels that make you bounce or speed along. Just as you’ve mastered one mechanic, it gives you a new one to combine with the rest. The puzzles are clever without being unfair and the moment a solution clicks makes you feel smart rather than just lucky.

The writing is the other big reason I love it. The characters are funnier and sharper than ever. The character voiced by J.K. Simmons steals every scene he’s in. The game is funny and it still manages to tell a surprisingly strong story with enjoyable twists and a fantastic ending.

The co-op campaign deserves its own praise. You have to plan, communicate and sometimes troll each other. It’s a solid and enjoyable co-op experience and feels like a whole second game.

The presentation holds up well too. The environments are full of detail, the soundtrack reacts to what you’re doing and the game runs well on almost any machine. Add years of community made levels and there’s a huge amount to enjoy.

Portal 2 is smart, funny and endlessly inventive. If you’ve never played it, it’s an easy recommendation.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes workshop support for creating and playing custom levels.

citations.review_text: Probably THE best puzzle game of all time. The mechanics and puzzles are satisfying, the story's quite memorable, and the replay value is almost endless thanks to its workshop support. Been a fan of this game for over a decade and I still can't get enough.

This is by far my favorite game of all time. Despite being from 2011 and being built on Source, which at launch was already a 7 year old engine, you don't really notice the age of the game too much. The portal mechanic was greatly extended from the first game with additional level elements, the story and its characters are downright iconic, the workshop provides even more levels, there are also mods like Portal Stories: Mel and Portal Revolution.

Honestly I don't even know much else to say about it.

Oh! it goes on sale all the time for maybe 2 dollars!

I probably like the inner workings even more because I was working on a dumb mod for it.
